title: Rectangular bar
spec: Create a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to -90.0 degrees, 0.0 degrees, and -90.0 degrees, and the translation vector set to 0.0, 0.0, and 0.0. On the first face, draw the first loop consisting of six lines. Start by drawing the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0278, 0.0), then the second line from (0.0278, 0.0) to (0.0278, 0.0278), followed by the third line from (0.0278, 0.0278) to (0.0261, 0.0278). Continue with the fourth line from (0.0261, 0.0278) to (0.0261, 0.0017), the fifth line from (0.0261, 0.0017) to (0.0, 0.0017), and finally the sixth line from (0.0, 0.0017) back to the origin (0.0, 0.0). Apply a scaling factor of 0.0278 to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it using the Euler angles -90.0 degrees, 0.0 degrees, and -90.0 degrees, and translating it using the translation vector 0.0, 0.0, and 0.0. Extrude the transformed two-dimensional sketch 0.75 units along the direction of the normal, ensuring no extrusion in the opposite direction. Create a new solid body using the extruded sketch. The final dimensions of the rectangular bar with rounded edges and a flat surface are 0.027777777777777776 units in length, 0.027777777777777776 units in width, and 0.7499999999999999 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0278, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0278, 0.0278) \
     .lineTo(0.0261, 0.0278) \
     .lineTo(0.0261, 0.0017) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0017) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define L-profile dimensions
L = 0.7500        # length along X
leg = 0.0278      # leg length of angle
t = 0.0125        # material thickness

# Build L-shaped angle: extrude along X
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(leg, 0)
    .lineTo(leg, t)
    .lineTo(t, t)
    .lineTo(t, leg)
    .lineTo(0, leg)
    .close()
    .extrude(L)
)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Equal-leg angle bracket (L cross-section) extruded along X
leg = 0.0278      # leg length in Y and Z
t = 0.007         # wall thickness of the angle
length = 0.75     # length along X

# Sketch the L profile on the YZ plane (Y right, Z up)
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(leg, 0)
    .lineTo(leg, leg)
    .lineTo(leg - t, leg)
    .lineTo(leg - t, t)
    .lineTo(0, t)
    .close()
    .extrude(length)
)
